I keep testing available models, and while all of them are immediately impressive in their facilities, I keep running into a wall of Dunning-Kruger confidence of statement/expertise when there are significant errors, including errors of omission, and I find these troubling, because someone who does not have certain domains of expertise could hear all the vocabulary from the AI, and because it sounds so confident, they accept the wrong answer.  
Even after pointing out errors, there's a pattern of, ego-less "so sorry, you are correct and ...". where the AI just goes on, continuing to present with extreme confidence as if the error(s) it made never happened.  
There's no sense of, "oops, thank you for correcting me.  I'll remember that, and source other references to confirm the validity and then make a permanent correction to my knowledge base so i never make that mistake again".
There's no sense of any self-awareness, even a simulated self awareness that would allow internal reflection and correction in a process of evolving self-correction, even red-teaming itself in virtual modeling and gaming to ensure future errors related to that domain of expertise do not occur as a proactive prep for future interactions on the same subject should the human continue that specific line of inquiry. 
This is expected with the free online AIs, but, it's the same with some of the largest competitive gguf AIs that can be run locally, and it's seen even in paid models.   
Anyway, as amazing as AI is with so very many things, I feel like we still have quite a way to go, unless there's a sudden growth in significant developmental sophistication.
